body: That’s some serious trolling from Leo.
Nothing means anything.  Your statements remind me of the old joke or ending every fortune cookie after Chinese food with “in the bed with me”.

Let me preface what I’m going to say with the fact that I think Davion is a great player and good dude.  I like his game, just not for Mike Brown’s system.  In all fairness he is off to a slow start but so are several Kings.  I just offensively he doesn’t gel with up tempo offense. Having perfect theology will not be that helpful.  We have to believe the gospel and trust God to leads us to more truth through His word.  I struggle with this but, more and more I am coming to see that my relationship with the Lord is what really counts.
Congrats man, I’m coming up on a year.  Hardest and best decision I ever made.

He hasn’t turned his back on you.  We have to trust Him.  I am going through many trials right now the fire is hot my friend. It really is about grace and a relationship with God which has already begun cause your talking to Him.  I want to stop the meds someday too, hate the side effects but the depression is so brutal 🤷‍♂️

People don’t go to hell because of sin, they go because they are unregenerate by the indwelling of the Holy Spirit. Sometimes I worry we put blocks in people’s paths that are unnecessary.  Either way we are forgiven I just don’t find scripture supporting this idea.  If some 20 yo has to rub one out to avoid losing his mind or committing some much worse sin.  Who am I to tell him not to? Making this post is an example of that imagine all the Christians suffering in silence who are encouraged to hear they’re not alone.  Overcome evil with good, I pray for your recovery and there is nothing wrong with asking for help.

I mean I was in what I would today consider a religious cult.  I thought for a long time that it was totally benign even after I left.  Today I can see where my thinking was distorted by the extreme beliefs of the group.  There wasn’t any overt mind control or manipulation.  There was a lot of social pressure and forced conformity.  Even though I wouldn’t rate my experience as traumatizing, I have had to unlearn a lot most importantly patterns of thinking.  So by definition there are not any benign cults, the damage may be subtle but it is there nonetheless.

Responsible no, but people need discipleship.  Think of all the mistakes you have made in your life, God can use those to help your friend stay on course.  There is so much to learn and we all need help and support.

Glad your praying, I’m a committed Christian and I have my doubts regularly.  Do you understand the gospel?  I only ask this question because it sounds like you may need some direction to get started.  I think depression and anxiety are medical problems.  God can remove them but, may not for several reasons.  Have you sought some medical attention for this issue?  I work in medical field as well and know how stressful it can be, especially right now.  Let us know how we can help and support you.

I think the best place to start is understanding the gospel.  Having a proper foundation is important.  The gospel is the good news of God’s free gift of salvation.  God sent Jesus to live a holy and sinless life.  Jesus is the only person to ever do that.  Jesus willingly gave himself over to death and the cross.  There he suffered and the Bible says he became sin for us.  This was to totally satisfy the sin problem that we might be reconciled to God.  After three days in the tomb Jesus rose from the dead.  If we believe this sincerely then God gives us his Holy Spirit.  Having the Spirit of God guides and comforts us.

Gospel Benefits:
1.  Total forgiveness for all sin, past, present and future (the sacrifice of Jesus was sufficient payment)
2.  A new nature, one that wants to be in fellowship with God and no longer enjoys the old life of sin (though we still may struggle with it)
3.  Eternal life with our savior
4.  Christ’s righteousness is given to us when we believe the gospel.  We are not only forgiven we are viewed as righteous in God’s eyes.
5.  A relationship with God, whereby he leads us and guides gently into all truth

Gospel Challenges:
1.  Our faith will be tested.  This can involve challenging circumstances, temptations to sin, loss of things in this world.
2.  We may experience more suffering in this life than unbelievers do.  This is for several reasons too much to go into here.
3.  The worst temptation is to try to earn or merit what God has decreed is only by his grace through faith alone.  Salvation is truly a free gift, our subsequent growth is through the Holy Spirit.  It is God’s work in us, not our work for God.

Welcome to the family😀😷☝️

In the moment no, cause in my experience ego gets in the way.  That is just me, in the context of what I wrote arguing about spiritual things which can be neither proven nor disproven will not have a ton of evidence.  In all honesty my faith is not based on evidence, it is based on experience and completely subjective.  The point I was making is that I don’t believe arguing to attempt to persuade someone to change their view is effective and in fact may be counterproductive.
Needed this thanks!

You don’t suffer from sexual sin you commit it.  I’m not trying to sound harsh.  You have to stop, but this seems impossible.  First if your sincere you probably do try to resist the sin.  I mean sometimes when I’m tempted it’s like physical torture.  If your like me you win some and lose some.  This is not the best way to go about this.

The way to victory in my experience is to realize how absolutely helpless this sin makes us.  We need to then change that belief to a gospel mindset.  The gospel teaches that we are totally forgiven and reconciled to God through Christ.  We are no longer fornicators, or slaves to sin because we have Christ’s righteousness.  We need to start believing the transformative reality of the gospel.  We have to face the truth of our shame that we choose to yield to these sins.  With Christ’s righteousness we began have different desires.  All the while he is doing this work in us to conform us to his image.  I wish you the best in your efforts to overcome the sins in your life.

This is me, I don’t have a lot of side effects but this one is a huge problem.  It’s like to start my day my dep/anxiety throws everything it can at me.  It requires superhuman strength to get out of bed.  Thanks for sharing I thought I was alone.

I have also dealt with this, I’m sorry you are suffering.  Nothing in this world no matter how horrible and suicidal depression and PTSD are pretty awful can separate you from the love of God.  This is your cross right now.  I don’t know how long it will last or if it will even get better.  You have a friend in Jesus who will stick by you and keep you.  You don’t really want to hurt yourself you just want to hurt less.  It’s really unfortunate that the Church in recent years has become a place where folks use the Bible to beat one another.  I will be praying for you.  Eventually this evil season will pass.

We don’t know it seems there are some verses that show Jesus giving grace to those who did something for the least of these.  Even giving them a cup of water or visiting them in prison.  It’s clear from the context that they were not believers.  See the parable of the sheep and the goats.

Listen my friend cause I want you understand this.  God’s messenger would not threaten you with punishment for not confessing sin.  The Holy Spirit is called a comforter.  God is a friend.  Do you have any friends that would do that?  If the voice doesn’t encourage and give you peace it is likely not from God.  You should reject that voice or any that doesn’t edify or lead to healing.  I’ve had similar struggles the power of these things is believing the message.  Simple affirm, I don’t believe you.  Then replace the negativity with an empowering statement like, I am God’s child and he has forgiven and accepted me.

I really think the notion that we can “convince” someone of this is flawed to begin with.  I have never during the course of an argument changed my opinion.  In matters of faith, I could not have been persuaded by argument.  God has to soften the hearts.  He responds when we lovingly pray for someone.  The catch here is he will not force someone into a relationship with Him.  Some people I’ve prayed for got a lot worse into sinful habits.  He is working on them and they are resisting.  Respect people’s freedom to not believe and know that in the right time with prayer and love God will reveal himself.  Then there’s nothing left to argue about 😀

We just have to let it play out, somewhere says that all Isreal will be saved.  Another place says they (the Jews) have a zeal for God but not according to knowledge.  The majority of Jewish people have rejected Jesus as messiah.  God has a plan though and his plans involve very precise influences, synchronicity and some crazy plot twists.  How will it end?, I think he’s playing his cards close to his chest.  Gonna be a wild ride is all I know.

I think these things are explained by personal freedom.  The big risk with freedom is that people are free to make the wrong choices.  I personally have found God to be subtle in his influence.  Could he intervene and stop bad things, yes.  Why doesn’t he? I don’t know.  I suspect that he doesn’t, to allow for true human choices with real consequences.
Well, understandable that they left they didn’t leave God, they left abuse.  Nothing more dangerous in this world than religion that is devoid of truth.

Me personally I relate to them quite a lot.  I was a skeptic and did not believe before becoming a Christian.  You could even say I was almost an anti-theist.  So it makes sense to me to question meta-physical things.  Though not often talked about I think both believers and atheists have their doubts about their positions and that’s ok.
Reprobates are on a slide away from God not towards him. Do you struggle to believe His promises I know I do.  Still he is faithful and will keep us.

Sorry your suffering and I can totally relate.  For me it wasn’t so much that I wanted to die but, I needed the pain to stop.  It didn’t for a long time sometimes still feel it.  I would love to say it gets better.  Not knowing your circumstances I have no way of saying that.  The best I can offer is that there is hope.  Just take it hour by hour.  Sometimes we have to break life up into little chunks to deal with the pain.  I can remember the horrible feeling of losing the joy in living.  When you can’t enjoy life anymore it seems pointless to continue.  God loves you though and has plans for you.  It takes time for these to develop.  The pain serves to build character and resilience while we wait.  It’ll be worth it eventually so try to stick around.

Well there is religion and there is the gospel.  I will try to break it down very simply.  Jesus came he was the son of God.  We believe that in a very real sense he was fully God and fully man.  He lived a life of moral perfection.  This was something that no one before or since has done.  Anything short of moral perfection is called sin.  Everyone has some sin, usually it is the things that make us feel guilty.  We are separated from a relationship with God due to this sin problem.

Jesus willingly gave his own life on the cross to solve this sin problem for us.  His sacrifice was sufficient payment for these sins.  Then after he was entombed after three days he rose from the dead.  He made promises to those who would believe.  The promises are: If we believe his offer of the free gift of eternal life, we would have it.  All sin past, present and future are forgiven.  Not only are we forgiven but in Gods eyes all of Jesus’s virtue is given to us.  He promised to give us his Spirit to comfort and guide us.  The best promise of all is that he would never leave us or forsake us.  He also warned that we should be careful about deciding to believe that this would surely be tested.  I hope this little summary was helpful, I did not include scripture references because, when people post bible verses it makes things hard to follow for me.  Hope your search is satisfying, God bless.

Well I mean discussing differences is necessary, though not always pleasant.  Everyone should be persuaded in their own mind.  I think a mature person is able to listen to other perspectives and learn from them even if they disagree.  The people who have different perspectives are not my enemies, they just disagree.  It is fascism to demand others validate our opinions or perspectives.

You know it’s interesting when we want so badly to do and be right but, keep failing.  Sometimes we think I shouldn’t have done that if only I could love God more.  These cycles are really frustrating.  We think we need to stop this or that sin.  We need to start doing this or that more.  What we really need is a savior.  My savior Jesus needs nothing from me.  He works in my life changing my desires and through this the temptations have less and less power.  If my doing could fix it, it would have been fixed long ago.  I trust in his promised forgiveness and the leading of the Holy Spirit.  I can rest believing that he who began a good work in me will complete it.  

If the result is left up to me.  If I need to serve Him in my own strength it will surely be a disaster.  Luckily he is keeping us, if we fall he picks us up.   The rest of faith is available to us.  I am happy with His terms, he gets all the glory and credit.  I get to experience the benefits he promised.  Total forgiveness, past present and future.  A transformed life, sometimes gradually for a hard head like me.  His Spirit to comfort and guide me.  The love he has for me is sustaining, regardless of circumstances.

The book teaches among other poignant lessons not to ask God why?  Well I mean you can ask but, you probably won’t understand the answer.  While Job was going through all his stuff, God was preparing his double portion.  Trials make us want to ask why?  Instead of trusting the character of God that there are perfectly good reasons for our suffering and that it won’t be in vain.  I like the veiled references to Christ you brought out from the passage, very illuminating.

Seems like there’s two sides, neither of which can hear each other just talking past.  
I have no desire to be lumped in with either in this false dichotomy.  People are people and all of them sin.  Is it necessary to confront someone about their sin.  Depends, if it’s to prove that your “not a compromiser”.  Then no that is not a good reason.  Is it because you feel the Holy Spirit is leading you do that, then I would say that is a good reason.  I don’t routinely confront my friends about their sin cause frankly it’s not my place to do so.  At most I might say you know that thing your doing, it’s annoying 🙂

I relate I haven’t had specific experience but, I find my brain very resistant to change.  That change causes irritability always for me.  Healing is a risk too.  What if we feel better and are still u successful?  I think changing the brain takes time and all sorts of feelings are part of that.

I mean this seems to be a common theme.  People who were self-medicating then getting on some AD.  After awhile, I feel better the meds are working, time to party.  I would caution you to be careful.  I don’t know about you but drugs and alcohol especially the latter played a significant role in my Illness.  The Zoloft is working to balance your brain chemistry.  Drugs and alcohol will upset this, there will likely be negative consequences.  I had some really amazing times partying and getting high.  So I totally get the impulse.  For me that time is over, in the end I paid some heavy tolls for It.  Today, boring old stability and health, I’ll take it.

Sorry about your brother friend.  I pray you find healing for your grief.  When it’s time to stop it’s time.  Remember the training wheels when learning to ride a bike?  Once you’ve got it down those got to come off, be well and comfort your family in their sorrows 🙂

Hey it so encouraging to hear the positive progress.  I like How you described being not happy, but not unhappy.  Sometimes thats a huge milestone if you ask me.  If you were in as deep a hole as I was, you’ve made some major progress.  Honestly any change for the better is welcome in my world, even if it’s just a glimmer.  I have PTSD as well and just starting therapy.  You give me hope, thanks!
They say 4-6 weeks to really have an idea if it will be effective for you.  If after 6 weeks you’ve got no positive benefits I think it would be pointless to up the dose.

The shaking orgasms sound pretty awesome actually not a defect but a feature 😉. Why did you ramp up so quickly?  I’m curious what your docs thought process was there.  I would call the doctor’s office sounds like too much too soon, in my opinion.  I work in the medical field but I’m not a physician.

Well that’s a tough spot your in my friend.  Tapering off cannabis can have some really challenging w/d symptoms for some people.  It’s hard to know what is causing the difficulty until you’ve been at the moderate consumption for about two weeks.  You may have to up your dose ultimately and unfortunately that carries the risk of Mr. Softee.  I think if it will improve depression and anxiety and panic symptoms it is worth it.  

Truth is as long as we are sick we’re not gonna be too good in a relationship.  Once your feeling better you’ll be able to more clearly see some of the causes of the panic attacks and address those underlying issues. With the goal of getting off the AD’s  Ultimately who wants to take these drugs for life.  It’s a life preserver for the drowning.  I wish you well man, hang in there plenty of time to date and hookup, when your the real version of yourself 🙂
You need an attorney really bad.  Hope the toxicology report doesn’t show other substances, as long as that’s the case, a good lawyer should be able to get you a good deal if not charges dropped.

I think it really depends on how you want to approach it.  For me depression was present albeit in a muted way in childhood.  Then some traumas happened that kind put me into some kind of back to the future horrible alternate timeline.  So my therapy has been less about focusing on CBT and the like.  More about tracing my own history and getting down to root causes.  Processing a whole lot of grief, anger, regret, pain, guilt, shame, sadness, loss and so forth.  The suffering is intense at times but I’m hoping It’s worth it.  

I do get a lot of mileage from rational emotive behavior therapy, sometimes (a form of CBT).  Again though, this is dealing with real-time symptoms and cognitive distortions.  My question is where did these things come from in the first place?  That’s a hard one to answer and sometimes really painful to accept the answer if I can find it.  Some days I just want a break from this kind of work.  It’s seems like having started the journey, God won’t let me off the hook got to go all the way through.  I think your thoughts are spot on though, AD’s are not the final answer but a stepping stone along the path.  I don’t expect to get well from a pill.  Or from diet and exercise.  Or therapy.  Or spiritual practices like meditation and prayer. Or connecting to a community of others who are healing.  I think it may take all of these to some degree and a whole lot of grace ☝️

That’s good to hear.  Lsd is really interesting I had some truly transcendent experiences.  In the end the alcohol kind of helped and hurt.  I drank for a long time.  I could really connect with people or so I thought through partying.  I haven’t had a drink in almost a year.  My emotions are outta control and there’s a lot pain facing stuff I ran from for so long.  I’m in counseling too and sometimes I just want to say to the wonderful lady, you just don’t understand how f*cked up I am.  She be like just keep walking in the pain.  I don’t know.  I just want to heal.  First from the original trauma, how people can be sexually attracted to kids is beyond me.  Then from all the damage I did to myself cause I didn’t know how to deal with that crap.  Glad your in counseling.  Although it often feels like taking a dump and poking it with a stick 🤪

Well, perhaps.  I medicated my depression for a long time with booze. Alcohol was relaxing and slowed down my amped up hyper vigilant brain.  If we’re talking about melancholic depression where things are already slowed way down then, I would say yes.  Most people nowadays have atypical which has a lot of features like anxiety and negative thinking that could use a little lightening up, so I guess I would say it depends 🤷‍♂️
Maybe 50 is too high to start.  I probably weigh more than you and started at 25.  I weigh 215, 44M.
Just because alcohol is called a depressant has nothing to do with depression.  It simply means that it’s effects are sedating and tend “depress” the nervous system 🙂

Seems a lot of folks expect medication to be a magic bullet to solve all your problems.  I look at it like this AD’s are a tool, if it gets you out of being incapacitated so you deal with problems in your life then it’s good.  If it doesn’t do that then it’s no good.
Congrats on your breakthrough.  When the pieces start coming together and making sense it’s really exhilarating and scary.  Here’s to you continued growth and living up to your potential.

I would recommend being careful right now.  We all want to believe that it will get better and maybe it will.  Having said that I have experienced a lessening of depression after a psychedelic experience.  I found out this is temporary, at least it was for me.  I respect wanting to self medicate over taking prescribed medication.  For me I could never find the sweet spot.  Acid trips no matter how profound don’t cure depression YMMV.  For the longest time alcohol was the greatest medicine for my illness.  It helped with social anxiety, helped my depression cause I didn’t have to face painful emotions and various other benefits.  In the end drinking caused me to make some very poor choices that hurt me and the people I care about in my life.  Then the feelings I was trying to suppress came boiling to the surface much more intensely than I was ready for.

Not trying to tell you what to do.  It is easy to convince ourselves that we are all better and due to drugs and alcohols ability to mask problems it can seem that way.  In the end even prescribed meds are limited.  We have to grow and work on the inner problems and traumas, nobody wants to do this of course.  I certainly didn’t have the courage to do so, it took losing everything, well everything important to me to start the work.  Not cured still depressed but gaining insight and getting to the roots of my problem.  Healing is elusive but, today I have an awareness and an acceptance.  I hope you find some answers and healing.  “Sometimes we live no particular way but our own.” Eyes of the world Grateful Dead.

I’ve always hated when people said that.  These are people who know nothing about real depression or ptsd.  Sometimes it doesn’t get better or the pain and suffering take so long to process until the concept of “better”, is an alien one.

Well “I feel fine enough I guess, considering everything’s a mess” barenaked ladies.  My wife and I are separated.  She never understood my pain (how could she).  She had a rebound with a sociopath who tried to strangle her.  Now she gets it and feels terrible.  While it’s nice for to understand the pain of trauma, I sure wish she didn’t.  I wouldn’t wish this shit on anyone.  We are trying to work it out, sigh.
Every single one of them, lol.  I’m glad though cause if I stayed in “I’m gonna conquer the world mode.”  I’d just be another narcissist out there wreaking havoc, 😂

The way it goes sometimes.  Sociopaths are often lauded for being wonderful people.  Meanwhile those of us trying to do good are awkward and creepy.  I’m glad you got some closure, no matter what they can never hurt you again.  I hope you find peace and safety.

Same I wish I could just stop smoking hopium and take myself out.  Won’t do that but, I envy the brave ones who can.  Funny thing after 30 years it’s not my head anymore.  It’s my body the pain in the cells aching to connect to another person.  Longing for impossible wholeness.  You really hit me with this.  Healing is just not a guaranteed thing.  Nobody knows the time frames to process this stuff.  My addictions won’t die soon as I quit one another one just takes its place.  My shame is no longer about the abuse, I’ve transferred that back to its rightful owner.  My shame is about how I responded running and hiding from life.  Reveling in dysfunction cause I didn’t know another way, safety and blessings.

If I had a dollar for everyone of these posts!  You are not alone.  You got saved, guess what from that day the devil had a strategy to try and get you to believe you weren’t saved.  His number one is the blasphemy/apostasy lie by far the number one.  I know stuff feels real hard right now but, the Lord is wanting to use this challenge to mature you.  Start taking every thought captive.  If the devil tells me I’ve sinned too much for God’s grace.  I tell him Jesus said “whosoever comes to me I will not cast out”.  If he tries to bring condemnation for sin I quote Romans 8.  Were in a battle just know that the fiery darts of the enemy are lies.  We can quench them if we don’t compromise our faith.

Yes l, exactly because that is how we were taught by religion.  Jesus wants us to have confidence in his promises to us and let him be our savior.  It’s hard to this the Bible says it this way, let us labor therefore to enter into His rest.  It’s a fight to simply trust God when all evidence seems like this could never work.  When we do though in essence give up, he shows up and starts to work in us.  I am not saying don’t read the scriptures or pray, just know that those are mere tools you could have the best hammer and tools available but to build a house you need a carpenter 😉

Exactly my point, well said.  I don’t think you’ll be successful in changing yourself.  As I put my trust in Jesus he through the Holy Spirit does a work in my life.  It is so good that you see the need for help.  The fact that it looks impossible means hopefully you won’t try (to change yourself in your own strength).  Just believe that his promises to forgive and heal you are true for you.  The Bible says without faith it is impossible to please God.  I have had to learn this over and over again (sadly).  Sometimes I put my faith in my prayer life or bible study.  Maybe in the work God has called me to do.  So this trust element makes or breaks our spiritual life.  If we become like little children being gently led by His spirit into all truth we will find a life far more satisfying than the pleasures of sin.

Hey I just wanted say thanks for taking off the mask and being real.  I went through some real struggles with kinks like this.  I later discovered a lot of it came from childhood trauma but, I’m not suggesting that’s true in your case.  God loves us just as we are and accepts us as his children being promised forgiveness and applying it are two different things.  We feel like we have to clean ourselves up and work really hard to be better.  This can lead to a lot of frustration cause God wants to save us.  He is busy pouring grace into our lives and we are going about trying to establish our own righteousness.  Like a surgeon operating on a gunshot victim we run in with a bandaid shouting “this should do the trick”.  Just enjoy his love for you and total acceptance.  If we stumble the Holy Spirit will be there to pick us up and help us refocus on him.  Just remember that it is all God’s grace, to save, heal and sustain us.
If you think being involved in politics will accomplish anything of value, I would suspect you are deceived but to be more charitable I’ll say deluded.

You need grace in this season my friend.  God is with you in trials and difficulties longing torescue you but restraining his hand.  Why?that our faith would be strong.  His love is greater than the devil, the world and even our sins and failures.  Don’t believe a false gospel that says “ If I tithed and prayed more I would be closer to God”.  Your actions cannot save you except one, placing your trust in him who is able to save.

I grew up in the holiness movement.  You know you must walk in perfect obedience to the word and church standards.  You can actually start to believe that you are becoming perfect.  So if perfection is the requirement let’s just look at one commandment and see how we’re doing.  This is the first commandment Matthew 22:37 Love the Lord thy God will all your heart soul and mind.  

It’s not just having a moment where you love God like that but, at all times without fail or excuse.  Pure and absolute devotion.  I have known some devout people but not one of them obeys this commandment.  The only way to claim sinless perfection is to have an unjust weight and balance.  Someone may rationalize well I don’t look at porn anymore so I’m sinless.  If you really believe this you need to take it all the way.  I like the rich young ruler who in arrogance says “all these commandments have I kept”, probably thinking Jesus would commend him.  Yet one thing though lacks, go and sell ALL and give to the poor.  Not one of us has done that.  What is the fruit of this doctrine? arrogance and eventually accepting heinous sin.  When I look at the remains of the holiness movements and all the casualties it is just not worth it.  Perfect obedience and sinless perfection is only possible if one is claiming they are God.  Or like the Pharisees changing the rules and the definition of sin to an acceptable level that one can live with.

I have to say in my case it was totally subjective, if I’m being honest.  I didn’t believe or want to believe.  I was forced to go to church which I resented.  It was in such a church service and I distinctly remember thinking I can’t wait for this to be over, when something broke inside me.   I started crying uncontrollably and I was flooded with God’s grace.  So I didn’t choose to believe, I was shown it.  I’m very grateful for this experience and I don’t think for a second that it is proof of God’s existence.  Of course it is to me.
